issues.detail: The Greek 'αὐτοῦ' (autou) refers back to a specific person/entity mentioned in the preceding context (likely Jesus or a specific figure), whereas the Vietnamese 'người ấy' (that person) is ambiguous. More importantly, the Greek 'ἀλλοτριω' (allotriō) is an imperative/exhortation ('let them not...'), while the Vietnamese 'sẽ không' (will not) renders it as a future prediction rather than a command or instruction.
